title: Finite locally constant sheaves and finite etale schemes
statement:
In the situation of [def-galois-categories], the functor

$$
\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\longrightarrow\mathrm{FLC}(Y),\qquad
P\longmapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P),
$$

where $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(T,P)$ is the set of
$Y$-morphisms $T\to P$, is an equivalence of categories. It is
compatible with base change and with the fibre functors, and it carries
$M$-torsors to $M$-torsors and simply transitive $M$-actions to
simply transitive ones.

proof.text: (The functor.) Let $P\to Y$ be an object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ [def-galois-categories], a finite etale $Y$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. By [lem-galois-flc-representable] (1) the presheaf $h_P=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P)$, $U\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}_Y(U,P)$, on $Y_{\Et}$ is a sheaf of sets and is finite locally constant: over the members $Y_i$ of a covering of $Y_{\Et}$ it is isomorphic to a constant sheaf with finite value $S_i$. So $h_P$ is an object of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$. A $Y$-morphism $g:P\to Q$ gives the morphism of sheaves $h_g:h_P\to h_Q$, $\varphi\mapsto g\circ\varphi$ (natural in $U$ because composition is associative), and $h_{g'\circ g}=h_{g'}\circ h_g$, $h_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; this is the functor $P\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P)$ of the statement.

(Full faithfulness.) A finite etale morphism is etale, so every object $P$ of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ is an object of the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and the morphisms $P\to Q$ in $Y_{\Et}$ are exactly the $Y$-morphisms, i.e. the morphisms of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. The morphisms $h_P\to h_Q$ in $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ are the morphisms of sheaves, i.e. the natural transformations of the underlying presheaves on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-galois-categories]. Hence the map $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(h_P,h_Q)$, $g\mapsto h_g=(g\circ-)$, of step 1 is the map of [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] for the category $\mathcal C=Y_{\Et}$ and the objects $P,Q$, and is therefore bijective, with inverse $\tau\mapsto\tau_P(\mathrm{id}_P)$. (This replaces the blueprint's argument by graphs and descent: no descent is needed for full faithfulness.)

(Essential surjectivity; the equivalence.) Let $\mathcal F$ be an object of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$, a finite locally constant sheaf of finite sets on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-galois-categories]. By [lem-galois-flc-representable] (2) there are a finite etale $P_{\mathcal F}\to Y$ and an isomorphism $\epsilon_{\mathcal F}:h_{P_{\mathcal F}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$. So the functor $h$ of step 1 is essentially surjective, and fully faithful by step 2. Written out: choosing $P_{\mathcal F},\epsilon_{\mathcal F}$ for every $\mathcal F$, a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ gives $\epsilon_{\mathcal G}^{-1}\alpha\epsilon_{\mathcal F}:h_{P_{\mathcal F}}\to h_{P_{\mathcal G}}$, which by step 2 is $h_{G(\alpha)}$ for a unique $Y$-morphism $G(\alpha):P_{\mathcal F}\to P_{\mathcal G}$; uniqueness gives $G(\beta\alpha)=G(\beta)G(\alpha)$ and $G(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Then $\epsilon:h\circ G\cong\mathrm{id}$ is a natural isomorphism by construction, and for $P$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ the isomorphism $\epsilon_{h_P}:h_{P_{h_P}}\to h_P$ is $h_{\eta_P}$ for a unique isomorphism $\eta_P:P_{h_P}\to P$ (step 2 applied to it and to its inverse), natural in $P$ by step 2 again. So $h$ is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse $G$.

(Compatibility with base change.) Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $P$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$; its base change $g^*P=P\times_YY'$ is in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Since $P$ is an object of $Y_{\Et}$ (step 2), [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable] with $f=g$, $X=Y'$, $V=P$ gives an isomorphism $g^{-1}h_P\cong h_{Y'\times_YP}=h_{g^*P}$ of sheaves on $Y'_{\Et}$, natural in $P$ for $Y$-morphisms. Thus the square formed by $h_Y$, $h_{Y'}$, base change $g^*:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\to\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$ and inverse image $g^{-1}$ commutes up to this natural isomorphism; in particular (with step 1 over $Y'$) $g^{-1}$ carries $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ into $\mathrm{FLC}(Y')$, every object of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ being some $h_P$ by step 3.

(Compatibility with the fibre functors.) Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be the geometric point of [def-galois-categories]. For $P$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, which is etale over $Y$, [lem-galois-stalk-representable] gives the bijection $(h_P)_{\bar y}\to|P_{\bar y}|$, $[(U,\bar u),\varphi]\mapsto\varphi\circ\bar u$, natural in $P$. So the fibre functor $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ composed with $h$ is naturally isomorphic to $P\mapsto|P_{\bar y}|$ on $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$.

proof.text: (Torsors and simply transitive actions.) Let $M$ be a finite abelian group; $M$-torsors on $Y_{\Et}$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors], read as torsors under the constant sheaf $\underline M$ in the sense of [def-sc-gm-torsor] (simply transitive action on the sections over every object, and sections locally; see the report on the missing local-nonemptiness clause of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors]). An $M$-torsor over $Y$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ is a finite etale surjective $P\to Y$ with an action of $M$ by $Y$-automorphisms for which $\coprod_{m\in M}P\to P\times_YP$, $(m+\cdot,\mathrm{id})$ on the $m$-th summand, is an isomorphism, as in [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor]. (a) By step 2, $g\mapsto h_g$ is a group isomorphism $\operatorname{Aut}_Y(P)\to\operatorname{Aut}(h_P)$, so actions of $M$ on $P$ by $Y$-automorphisms correspond bijectively to actions of $M$ on the sheaf $h_P$, and such an action of $M$ extends to the action of $\underline M$ of [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor] (a locally constant $a$ acting by $m$ on $a^{-1}(m)$). (b) Torsors to torsors: if $P$ is an $M$-torsor over $Y$, then $h_P$ with this action is a torsor under $\underline M$ by [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor] (1), and it is finite locally constant by step 1; the map $\underline M\times h_P\to h_P\times h_P$, $(a,\varphi)\mapsto(a\cdot\varphi,\varphi)$, is bijective on sections over every $U$ because for each $\varphi$ the map $a\mapsto a\cdot\varphi$ is bijective. (c) Conversely let $T$ be a torsor under $\underline M$. By [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor] (2) $T$ is finite locally constant, with finite values $M$, so by [lem-galois-flc-representable] (2) its underlying sheaf is isomorphic to $h_Q$ for a finite etale $Q\to Y$, and by [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor] (3) there is an action of $M$ on $Q$ making $Q$ an $M$-torsor over $Y$ with $h_Q\cong T$ as torsors. So up to isomorphism the torsors under $\underline M$ are exactly the $h_P$ of the $M$-torsors $P$ over $Y$. (d) Simply transitive actions: let $P\to Y$ be finite etale with an action $m\mapsto(m+\cdot)$ of $M$ by $Y$-automorphisms. If $P$ with it is an $M$-torsor, $h_P$ with the corresponding action is a torsor under $\underline M$ by (b). Conversely, if $h_P$ with the corresponding action is a torsor $T$ under $\underline M$, (c) applied to $T$ and the identity $h_P\cong T$ gives an action $m\mapsto(m+'\cdot)$ making $P$ an $M$-torsor and an isomorphism of torsors $h_P\to h_P$ from the $+'$-action to the $+$-action; by step 2 it is $h_\psi$ for a $Y$-automorphism $\psi$ of $P$, and compatibility with the constant sections gives $\psi\circ(m+'\cdot)=(m+\cdot)\circ\psi$ for all $m$ (step 2 again). Hence $P\to Y$ is surjective and the morphism $\coprod_mP\to P\times_YP$ for $+$ is the one for $+'$ conjugated by the isomorphisms $\coprod_m\psi$ and $\psi\times_Y\psi$, so it is an isomorphism: $P$ with the given action is an $M$-torsor.
